content.comment_body: Hello, I'm using the astronomic clock block in [product_name] to control courtyard lighting. Strangely, the output signal sometimes inverts—lights turn on during the day and off at night. If I invert the output pin, it works for some time before the inversion happens again. The clock and latitude/longitude settings are correct, and my device isn't connected to LAN. Has anyone encountered this issue?

This is the first time I've heard of this issue. It suggests that the programming could be changing on its own. Could you upload your program as a zip file? Also, which [product_name] model and firmware version are you using?

Thank you, [user_name]. My device is a [product_name] with firmware [version_no]. The night light worked for two months, then the output inverted for five days before returning to normal, all without any programming or installation changes. I don't have a computer cable and programmed directly on the device's interface; the schematic is simple: AC -> NOT -> Q3, and Q3 controls the night light. The output switches at the correct times but I occasionally have to invert the NOT block for it to function properly. I hope you can assist.

The astronomic clock uses longitude, latitude, and time zone to determine sunrise and sunset times. The output is active between these times. To switch a light on at night, you must invert the output using a NOT block. I haven't encountered cases where the clock's output behavior changes for several days unexpectedly. For an official explanation, consider submitting a Support Request.

That's unusual. I've completed several projects using the astronomic clock feature without issues. Using [product_name] programming software to create and download the program is best, allowing you to post your program for review.

I've used the astronomic clock in multiple projects, including in my home to control several lights, both automatically and manually. I've never seen this issue. If you don't want to purchase the full programming software, you can download a demo version to test your setup on a PC. Also, ensure both the device's clock and date are set correctly.

Thank you for your input! After 10 days of normal operation, the output inverted again—now the AC output is off between sunrise and sunset, contrary to specifications. I have the programming software and other installations, but don't see how it could resolve this simple case. Registering a support ticket takes a lot of time, and in my experience, doesn't produce results. When experienced users can't answer, support likely won't either and may just ask for repair or replacement. As my device also controls ventilation and is out of warranty, that's not an option. I may need to switch to something else like a Sonoff.
Greetings, does anyone else have access to your [product_name]? Please upload your program for us to review.
Is your [product_name] using a micro-SD card? Is the program also saved on that SD card?
Hi, perhaps the [product_name] hardware is malfunctioning.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members describe a recurring issue with the astronomic clock function in [product_name], where output inverts and causes outdoor lighting to operate incorrectly for several days before returning to normal. The main user sees this inversion happen without changes to programming or settings. Other users note that this behavior is atypical, based on their own experience, and suggest general troubleshooting steps, but no definitive solution is identified.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the astronomic clock function in [product_name] to perform consistently, reliably switching lighting according to sunrise and sunset times. They want the output logic to remain stable unless changed manually.
